f08_resolution.fix: the instrumented runner owns its iteration loop and records retry_event, retry_count, retry_seed, nan_detected, stopping_reason and actual_iterations. In production on_nan=fail: a NaN latent sample raises RetryDetected instead of restarting, and the sweep turns that into a fit failure. A restart re-seeds with seed+1000, so its first iterations are no longer the ones the archived baseline took and the pairing for that fit is void -- treating it as a failure is the honest handling, not an inconvenience.
f08_resolution.problem: em_runner resets nan_count at the top of every retry and breaks on the first clean attempt, so an internal NaN restart is invisible in the returned counters

not_recorded_and_why.gradient_norm: the E-step Newton solve does not return its gradient; exposing it would change the model classes, which are shared with the historical lineage
not_recorded_and_why.held_out_score_per_iteration: recorded only at checkpoints, deliberately -- a per-iteration held-out trace invites using it as a stopping signal, which would be leakage

checkpoint_invariance.claim: checkpoint evaluation consumes no randomness, mutates no optimiser state, and does not change the trajectory of a long run
evidence: I3: a 40-iteration run evaluated at six checkpoints ends bit-identically to one evaluated only at iteration 40
I2: checkpoint 8 of a 40-iteration run equals the whole of an 8-iteration run
I1: the instrumented runner reproduces em_runner exactly at the baseline budget
the criterion functions take no rng and are deterministic (verified by reading them)

convergence_diagnostics.budget_stable_at_tau: max gram_rel_change over the last 4 iterations before the checkpoint < tau
convergence_diagnostics.denominator_choice: mixed absolute-relative, 1 + |x| rather than |x| + eps: a pure relative change explodes when a parameter passes near zero, which for w and w0 is an ordinary event, not a signal.
convergence_diagnostics.f_raw_change: ||F_t - F_{t-1}||_F / (1 + ||F_{t-1}||_F). Recorded, but MUST NOT be used on its own to call a fit stable: it counts rotation as movement.
convergence_diagnostics.gram_rel_change: ||F_t F_t^T - F_{t-1} F_{t-1}^T||_F / (1 + ||F_{t-1} F_{t-1}^T||_F). The latent space is identified only up to an orthogonal transform, so F itself can move a long way between iterations without the fitted distribution moving at all. F F^T is invariant to that rotation and therefore measures the part of the change that is real.
convergence_diagnostics.monte_carlo_floor_caveat: L=5 latent draws are redrawn every iteration, so none of these decays to zero at a fixed point. Every one of them is therefore a statement about the size of the Monte-Carlo jitter as much as about convergence, and the jitter may itself depend on K. This design does not resolve that; it declares it.
convergence_diagnostics.purpose: descriptive budget-stability only; not a formal convergence proof
convergence_diagnostics.tau_ladder_note: ALL THREE are reported. No single tau is designated the convergence threshold, because choosing one after seeing the results is exactly what this preregistration prevents.

held_fixed_from_baseline.model_seed_formula: MODEL_SEED_BASE + k_true*100000 + n*1000 + replicate*100 + k_est*10 + start
held_fixed_from_baseline.seed_bases_source: read from the baseline protocol.json, never retyped
held_fixed_from_baseline.selection_aggregation: unweighted mean over the two starts

implementation.em_runner_unchanged_note: expfam/src/experimental/em_runner.py is byte-unchanged. The instrumented loop is a separate module that mirrors it line for line; equivalence is measured (probe I1), not assumed, and is re-proved on the real cells by the replication gate.
tests: tools/research_audit/_em_budget_probe.py (child process; the Phase 8b suite forbids importing an EM runner into the test process)

A.forbidden: must not be reported as 'the criteria work after all' -- it says the 8-iteration result was budget-limited, nothing about consistency
A.pattern: delta_K increases with K and selected K moves toward K_TRUE at longer budgets
A.reading: evidence for fixed-budget optimization confounding; the baseline under-selection may NOT be attributed to the criteria

B.forbidden: must NOT be reported as proof that the cause is the criterion; L, the MC floor and the initialisation remain uncontrolled
B.pattern: objective and convergence diagnostics improve but selected K is essentially unchanged
B.reading: under-selection is not explained by the 8-iteration truncation alone

C.forbidden: must not be generalised beyond K_TRUE=5 and these three n
C.pattern: high-K fits are already budget-stable at iteration 8
C.reading: the F-02 optimization explanation is weakened for this setting

D.forbidden: the word 'improvement' must not be used in any direction
D.pattern: longer optimization destabilises selection or increases over-selection
D.reading: optimization and criterion interact; report as an interaction, not as degradation

interpretation_matrix.meta: All four are scientific results. K=5 failing to win more often is NOT a failed experiment, and no outcome may trigger a protocol change, a re-run, a seed change or an added arm.

optimization_budget.adaptive_stopping_note: There is NO adaptive stopping rule. Every candidate K receives exactly the same number of iterations, so a stopping rule cannot favour or disfavour any K. Convergence is measured and reported, never used to stop, and never used to select K.
optimization_budget.intermediate_checkpoints_are_secondary: 12/16/24/32 describe the trajectory only. 40 is a BUDGET: it is never called converged, in the artifact, in the report or in any claim.
optimization_budget.rationale: One run of 40 iterations costs 40 iterations; running 8/12/16/24/32/40 separately costs 132. The prefix property that makes the two equivalent is asserted in tools/research_audit/test_em_budget_nesting.py (N1) and is verified against the archive by the replication gate.

pilot.freeze_rule: The protocol is hashed and frozen BEFORE the pilot runs. The pilot may only return PASS or FAIL; it may not change any protocol field. If a field would have to change, the protocol is re-frozen as a new version and the pilot is re-run in full.
pilot.name: replication gate
pilot.on_fail: BLOCKER. Production is not authorised. Do not adjust tolerances, do not switch to approximate comparison, do not proceed with an unpaired design.
pilot.pass_condition: for all 14 fits, heldout_mean_log_score, q_strict, s2_q_based, s3_plugin_conditional and num_params are EXACTLY equal (bit-identical float repr) to the corresponding rows of the archived fit_results.csv, and train/test mask hashes match mask provenance
pilot.purpose: prove that the new instrumented runner reproduces the archived baseline exactly at checkpoint 8, so that the paired comparison is a comparison of budgets and not of code paths
pilot.restrictions: the gate is used ONLY for runtime confirmation, replication and instrumentation correctness. Its selected K and its recovery counts must not be looked at, and may not change max_iter, the checkpoints, the candidate K set, the replicates, n or the stopping rule. If runtime exceeds the pre-set abort threshold, the run stops and goes back to human review; it does NOT shrink itself.
pilot.scope: K_TRUE=5, n=75, replicate 1, all 7 candidate K, both starts

primary_outcomes.comparison: checkpoint 8 versus checkpoint 40, paired within replicate
primary_outcomes.definition: selected K per (criterion, n, replicate) at each checkpoint, with the frozen selector unchanged
primary_outcomes.name: selected K by budget

primary_outcomes.comparison: is delta_K increasing in K? Reported as the full table plus the Spearman correlation between K and delta_K within each n. Descriptive only: 7 points, no inferential claim, no p-value threshold.
primary_outcomes.definition: delta_K = mean S1 held-out score at checkpoint 40 minus at checkpoint 8, for each candidate K
primary_outcomes.name: per-candidate-K score gain from extra iterations
primary_outcomes.note: This is the outcome that most directly separates the two explanations.

protocol.estimand: under the same data, masks, initialization and first-eight-iteration RNG prefix, how does continuing the same L=5 stochastic MCEM procedure from iteration 8 to iteration 40 change the selected-K pattern

P1.comparison: checkpoint 8 versus checkpoint 40, paired within replicate
P1.definition: for each (n, replicate) and each checkpoint: average S1 over the two starts for every candidate K, take the K with the largest average; tie tolerance 1e-12, ties resolved to the smallest K
P1.name: selected K by budget
reported: exact / under / over counts at each checkpoint

P2.definition: delta(n, r, K) = 0.5 * sum over start in {1,2} of [ S1(n, r, K, start, 40) - S1(n, r, K, start, 8) ]
P2.inference: DESCRIPTIVE ONLY. No formal test. Spearman between K and the mean delta may be shown as a diagnostic; the 7 candidate K are NOT independent samples and no p-value is reported
P2.name: per-candidate-K S1 change from continuing the procedure
reported: all 8 replicate-level deltas for every (n, K), not only a mean

secondary: winning margin (best minus runner-up in selector space) by checkpoint
budget-stability rates by candidate K and n at every tau
S2 and S3 versions of P1 and P2
primary_outcomes.wording: no materiality threshold is defined, so the question says CHANGES, not 'materially changes'

protocol.residual_confound: continuing the procedure redraws L=5 latent samples every further iteration, so additional optimization and additional Monte-Carlo variation are not separable by this design

replication_gate.agreement_rule: EXACT equality on every compared field
replication_gate.agreement_rule_justification: csv writes Python floats with repr, which round-trips through float() without loss, so bit-identical comparison is technically achievable for every compared field. No tolerance is defined, because a tolerance here would only be a place for a real discrepancy to hide. runtime_s is excluded: it is wall-clock and is not reproducible.
replication_gate.cell_selection_rule: the first replicate of the smallest scoped n. Fixed by rule, written down before the gate was ever run, and derived in code as min(N_GRID) so it cannot be quietly re-picked.
replication_gate.on_fail: PRODUCTION AUTHORIZATION = NO. Stop. Do not loosen the comparison, do not switch to a tolerance, do not fall back to an unpaired design.
replication_gate.post_production_recheck: the auditor re-compares checkpoint 8 of ALL fits in the final scope against the archive, so the guarantee is re-established over the whole run and not only over the gate cell (audit check replication_vs_baseline, BLOCKER on any mismatch).
replication_gate.purpose: prove the new code path reproduces the archived baseline exactly at checkpoint 8, so the paired comparison compares budgets and not implementations
replication_gate.selection_inputs_covered: S1, S2 and S3 raw values plus num_params are exactly the inputs the frozen selector consumes, so agreement on them means selected K is reproduced by construction.

research_question: Does relaxing the fixed 8-iteration optimization budget materially change the selected-K pattern under the otherwise frozen clean-generator protocol?

runtime_estimate.abort_threshold: if elapsed time exceeds 2x the projection, stop and write failure.json; do not resume
runtime_estimate.checkpoint_overhead_note: six checkpoint evaluations per fit instead of one final evaluation; each costs one Q_strict, one held-out score and one S3 pass, all deterministic. Budget an additional allowance rather than assuming it is free.

n50_addition.note: computed from the archive alone by run_em_convergence_sensitivity.py --plan-n. Adding n=50 costs +0.74 h (+14%) and removes the result-informed-n criticism, because {50,75,100,150} is then the baseline's whole n grid rather than a subset chosen after seeing which n under-selected.
n50_addition.recommendation: adopt n = {50,75,100,150}. NOT changed here: scope is a human decision at freeze.

runtime_estimate.projection_method: linear in iteration count; conservative because each fit also pays a fixed end-of-run cost that does not scale

alternative_under_review.status: recommended, awaiting human decision at protocol freeze

excluded.k_true_1: confounded three ways in the baseline (floor of the candidate set, under-selection dominance, heaviest-tailed signal); it cannot discriminate between the two explanations
excluded.k_true_3: only 4 replicates per cell; the budget contrast would rest on half the sample of K_TRUE=5
excluded.n_50: n=75 already shows the strongest under-selection in the baseline (S1 exact 0/8 versus 2/8 at n=50), so n=50 is not the extreme case and adds a fourth point without adding a contrast. Recorded here BEFORE any new fit exists.

scope.replicate_selection: ALL 8 replicates of every scoped cell; no subsetting, so no cherry-picking rule is needed
scope.scope_is_result_informed_note: The choice of K_TRUE=5 and of these three n IS informed by the baseline result. This is unavoidable -- the question is about that observed under-selection -- but it means this experiment is a targeted follow-up, not an independent test. The rule is fixed here, before any new data exists, and no outcome may change it.
